decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "To make the default safe for multi-threaded use, set `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` plus either `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` or `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT`." | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the macros that gate the threading and mutex code.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out in `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787` (`//#define MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`). Neither `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` nor `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` is enabled either (lines 2185, 2196)." | WHY: The answer says the shipped config leaves THREADING_C commented out and neither PTHREAD nor ALT enabled, so a default build defines none of them. The item asks for the two threading macros, and PTHREAD and ALT are the ones that matter here.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "with the default configuration, the library starts no threads and takes no locks." | WHY: The answer says the library creates no threads by default, but it never says the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`library/` contains no `pthread_create`, `std::thread` or `_beginthread`. The library never creates a thread." | WHY: The answer states that the library creates no threads, but it never says library/ supplies the mutex abstraction (threading layer) for threaded callers. It only says mutex code is compiled out by default and tells users to enable `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` with PTHREAD or ALT.
